title: Not very effective on gnats. Bone dry in 19 days.
body: The traps caught a few gnats for a few days - then nothing. Mine are bone dry after 19 days - nowhere near the 45 days claimed. I guess the attractive containers could be used with a vinegar and dish soap mix, but the plastic tub with a 4" diameter open top I used before getting these caught more gnats. My recommendation would be to spend your money on a large bottle of apple cider vinegar and plan to refresh your bait every week.

I've been using a "recipe" I found online for a few years now to get rid
of fruit flies every time these darn things start popping up- a mixture
of apple cider vinegar, sugar, dish soap, and water. It works AMAZINGLY
every time. Seems lately however, I can't keep up with refilling the
dish, changing out the mixture for new stuff (they're SO BAD right
now!!). I was attracted to this stuff by its cute little apple
container, and the fact that it claimed to last 45 days. Well, it's been
less than a week and I've already gone through all 4. They don't seem to
work as well as the DIY mixture I make, nor do they seem to attract as
many fruit flies as when I just put the mixture in a small bowl.
Should've known it wouldn't work as well, but with all of the great
reviews, I was hopeful! Just Google the "recipe" to make the stuff on
your own. It's a lot cheaper!

title: Greenway traps are better than Terro
body: Greenway traps each caught a dozen fruit flies in a couple of days. The only downside is that they don't catch other species of small bugs. (For those pour bleach down the drain.) My Terro traps caught only a few before the liquid evaporated. The Greenway bottle design keeps them from spilling, and also from evaporating. Terro traps have several big holes so they can spill, and that also allows the liquid to evaporate faster. Terro comes with refills but Greenway doesn't need them. The bugs can also get out of the Terro as easily as getting in, but the Greenway traps hold them until the fumes kill them. They can't climb out with the funnel opening for the same reason it doesn't spill.

body: It may work with fruit flies, but it doesn't work with gnats.

DOES NOT WORK. I have a gnat infestation in my indoor office plants.
Because they are in my office, where I spend 8 hours per day, I needed
them gone, stat. I tried 3 different methods of gnat elimination: (1)
Terro apple-shaped fly traps; (2) Shallow dishes of liquid dish soap;
(3) Zevo plug-in flying insect trap.

After 3 days, here are the results:

\(1\) Terro apple-shaped fly traps: Easy to set up and fill with their
"special" gnat-attracting formula which I am sure is just apple cider
vinegar. The apple containers are small and cute. But, they don't work.
I CAUGHT 1 (ONE) GNAT using 4 different traps placed on top of soil in
my plant containers.

\(2\) Shallow dishes of dawn dish soap: Easy to set up and fill.
However, the liquid soap starts to dry out and harden after several
days. They are a bit of a pain to wash out and refill, icks me out, plus
I think it's a waste of dish soap. I CAUGHT 50 GNATS using this
method--I used 4 different shallow containers placed on top of soil in
my plant containers.

\(3\) Zevo plug-in flying insect trap. This plug-in fly trap was super
easy to set up. It's basically a blue light that attracts the insects
and super sticky paper (comes with replacement inserts) to trap them. I
CAUGHT 40 GNATS using this method. This trap is the furthest from my
plants--it's about 6 feet away. If I move it closer, it will probably
work even better. This is my favorite scent-free, mess-free method that
actually works.

If I didn't use the other 2 methods, I would have about 100 more gnats
still flying around my office space, ick. Save your money and don't
buy.

title: Poor design, spills easily!
body: I was expecting more for the extra money I spent on this Raid product. Like maybe a liquid product that wouldn't spill stuff all over when I opened it. When I unscrewed the lid, Raid had one of those protective plastic coverings over the opening of the jar that you have to peel back by gripping the extra piece of attached material that's supposed to make it easier to peel, but doesn't actually WORK since it's glued on so firmly. Oh well. OK. So I grabbed a sharp knife and carved away the temporary protective covering, which exposed the jar of apple cider vinegar that is said to kill the fruit flies. For the price, I expected another lid with holes in it to prevent it from spilling when I put it down near my compost pail. But no. It was just a jar of open liquid that had already spilled once when I carved away the protective covering! So I had to place the $8.18 jar of Raid in a sealed plastic sandwich bag with holes in it. I don't know yet how well it works. But here's the issue. If I wanted to create a DIY fruit fly disposal system, I would get my own jar of apple cider vinegar and put it in a sealed sandwich bag with holes in it. AND I would have saved myself $8.18! There are other, better designed fruit fly apple cider products on Amazon that have holes in the lids to prevent spillage. I just expected more from a big brand name like Raid. Silly me.

title: Didn’t work at all…. Perhaps it was the bug not the product?
body: This is a long story. I bought canned cat food from Amazon, as usual I put it in the cupboard and went on with life. Fast forward, a few days later little bugs started flying around my kitchen, I thought they were fruit flies. For two days I put up with them then bought this. Basically this is apple cider vinegar mixed with sugar. You can make the recipe yourself, which I would do instead of buying this. Now, upon a week after the food was put in the cupboard I opened it and was attacked by these little bombers with wings. The gray of cat food was infested, hundreds with eggs. The can of food in the second tray which was covered with the standard cardboard and outer plastic was split which made a great environment for these little jerks. It took me a week to hand kill these things- thankfully they were slow. Perhaps they were not fruit flies and that is why this product didn’t work. This is not why I am giving it two stars. I am giving it 2 starts because of its application. Once the top is flipped open it is easy to tip over, it is not balanced. The top is completely open because the goal is for the flies to go in for a drink and drown. Well, unless you put this inside a mug it is very easy to accidentally tip over. The smell is nauseating, but that is not the fault of the product, sometime the “medicine” is just awful. I also think it is a little overpriced. $8. For ingredients that would cost at most $.75. I know it is the ease of use and when you are being overtaken by bugs you are willing to pay anything. I am giving it 3 stars because I am indifferent of its effectiveness. I am not sure if these were fruit flies- if they were, then this product didn’t work at all, if they weren’t then I am judging the other aspects of the product: ease of use, quality, cost. Etc. Quality: Nice looking label, The high pungent smell of vinegar is enough to make you gag- so, it is the real deal and not watered down. Ease of use: just peel off the thin protective film and flip open the lid- voila. Cost: I think it’s a little pricey for the ingredients which you could easily make yourself. (They give the recipe online) But, isn’t it easy to press the “buy now” button and have the delivery guy drop at your door 48 hrs later?

title: Works but shouldn't be your only method
body: I had a bad infestation of fruit flies, worse then I have ever experienced this year. Fruit flies can come into your house on produce or they can develop in your drains. The product does work but if you have an infestation of fruit flies you must use several methods to exterminate them which takes time and patience.1. Throw ALL food you keep on your counters. This not only includes fruit but any other food you keep out. Fruit flies are attracted to fermenting foods. I had a mesh bag full of onions in my lazy Susan that I had to throw out because I found the flies in the bag.2. Deep clean your entire kitchen. The fuit flies continue the reproduce because they are laying their eggs on surfaces that are dirty. They can lay up to 500 eggs a day so if the adults keep having places to land aka fruit and sticky surfaces they will continue to reproduce. This means taking out everything on your counter and spraying with a cleaner solution.3. Last but not least, you need to find the source! Fruit flies can breed in your kitchen drain. This means using a solution to pour down the drain to kill the flies and eggs. There is solutions sold on Amazon that can be used. This needs several treatments and ensure your sink is always clean.In conclusion, you can get ride of fruit flies but it takes time. For me it took about 2 weeks. If you only use this trap, its just catching the flies but they will still reproduce if you don't give them a place to breed. Along with these traps, I made my own with apple cider vinegar. I deep cleaned my kitchen and bought the solution used to treat the sink for flies. One you kill the breeding ground, you just continue to set traps until the last adults are gone.Good Luck!

Someone gave us a bag of ripe fruit and all of a sudden we had fruit
flys everywhere! I read a bunch of reviews and ordered these Terro fruit

These are the best. I had a fruit fly problem that I couldn't get rid
of. I tried the cups filled with brandy or fruits and it never seemed to
catch all the flys. I put these in every room and we were getting fruit
flys in places we didn't even know we had them. The only issue is that I
need more of the inside juice because it does evaporate over time and I
didn't realize I should save some of the juice to refill later.

It's always a bit of an unknown trying something new like this, but it
sure did the trick. No, not of its own, but as 1 element in a multiprong
attack, this has made a huge difference. I keep a compost bucket in the
kitchen for all organics the dogs can't eat, so it has its own little
fan club, and they can get out of control pretty darn quick. This has
been worth it so far.

Lately, we've been buying more fruit than usual. Something we brought
home must have had a few fruit flies or eggs, so we've got some of the
pesky critters flying around in the kitchen. It's not a big
infestation, but I do see maybe a half dozen of them a day. So, I've
tried a couple of things.

I made a couple of do-it-yourself traps. There are a couple of them on
the internet. It's apple cider vinegar in a mason jar with small holes
in the lid (or a cup with plastic wrap with holes). I made both, and
caught a few flies.

Then I bought the Terro traps. They are cute and inexpensive. I'm
pretty sure the magic "attractant" is apple cider vinegar with some
kind of surfactant to make sure the critters don't float when they hit
the liquid. I'm guessing a drop of dish wash detergent would work for
that purpose. These also caught a few flies. On several occasions, I've
seen them land on the lid and walk around for a while and then fly away.
I don't know why they don't go inside the holes - one of life's great
mysteries.

Then I bought a trap with blue light and sticky paper. This also caught
a few.

The most effective (and most fun) is to use our Dyson stick vacuum. We
have white cabinets, so it's easy to see the files when they land.
I've observed that they tend to like vertical surfaces and generally
orient themselves head-up. They also take off backwards. So, if you get
the vacuum running on high and sneak up on them from below, you can
generally suck them in. At least for me, this has some entertainment
value. My wife tells me that I remind her of Bill Murray in Ghostbusters
with that thing. But it definitely does work. Who you gonna call\...?

Bottom line\... I haven't found any magic solution to the problem.
Everything seems to work about equally well. I have my homemade traps,
the Terro traps and the light trap all deployed. There is some value in
purchasing the Terro traps, because they are the most attractive option.
They are also inexpensive. They look like little apples. Don't get hung
up on their "attractant". Apple cider vinegar and dishwasher detergent
should be an effective substitute.

Happy hunting!
Works good but on the small size. Cute apple design

in droves.

Placed 2 Terro fruit fly traps near the trash and by the window - by the
end of second day, the number of flies came down to couple of dozen.

To add to this I had also set up a few sticky fly traps in the plant
pots - they caught a few

1 week in, there are very few flying around. Though I have to say - this
liquid that you need to pour in, does stink like apple cider vinegar and
something else.

They work relatively well. The lure they come with attracts fruit flies
and kills them rather nicely. On the plus side, it's small, so easy to
hide. However, and it's a big one (at least to me). The lids are so
hard to remove. They are snap-on lids (instead of twist-on), so with a
bunch of dead bugs in the container, you have to force the lids off, and
in the process, you can get dead bugs on your hands. I will never buy
these again.

title: Amazingly effective!
body: We've been having a serious fruit fly/gnat infestation for years, and I'm almost positive they're breeding somewhere in our walls, floors or ceilings -- we've had leaks in the past, and I think we still do. So while it may take more than a trap to eradicate the gnat population here, this trap has brought us substantial relief, in just the span of 2-3 days.We can't call in the professionals at this point, for reasons I can't go into, but since the weather got warmer this spring, life in our small apartment was becoming unbearable. They were flying into our faces, landing on us, and landing in or on our food, even as we prepared it or ate it.I don't think it's been more than 48 hours, and there are A LOT of dead flies in the trap.We've caught substantial numbers with both homemade vinegar traps and the electronic Katchees, but this trap seems to summon the gnats, even from other rooms of the apartment (the trap is in the bedroom, but we also have a combination kitchen/LR, a bathroom and a foyer).Be warned, the trap does have a strict vinegar smell that wafts around, but the smell is NOTHING in comparison to the nuisance of the gnats.They do hang around the rim of the trap for a while, but then they definitely fly into it and die. We put it in an awkward place, and I don't want to take the chance of spilling it, so I can't get anything close to a count, but not only can I glimpse a large quantity of dead gnats, but I haven't seen ANY flying or landing anywhere else in our place, in many hours. This is truly amazing.I don't expect that it will eradicate them completely, because we don't know the breeding source, but one can always hope that all breeding adults will eventually fly around and find this thing. Until then, we may have to keep replacing the traps and finding ways to stretch out the liquid. Maybe we'll post an update, at some point.Meanwhile, I THANK GOD for the blessing of having this trap to control the terrible nuisance that was making our lives so unpleasant and difficult.Posting this update about 2-3 weeks later -- unfortunately in the warm weather (and we don't have air conditioning), these gnats are multiplying faster than the trap can catch them. Without it, we'd probably be swamped in gnats, fruit flies and whatever all these pests are. We'll have to put more traps around.

title: I was extremely dissappointed in this product
body: I read the directions twice and it is very simple. Shake real good before opening then unscrew the lid off and peel off the protective foil. Then just leave it sitting out on a counter or whatever, near where the fruit flies or gnats seem to be the worse. I would watch the fruit flies crawl all over this product kinda checking it out but it seemed they would always lose interest and go away instead of going for the liquid to get trapped. Now to be fair, I may have caught close to 50 after a couple weeks but when I saw it wasn't working to well, I broke out some fly ribbon paper I had leftover in an old box and the fly ribbon was absolutely covered with them so I won't be wasting any more money on traps like this when I can get 10pc of fly ribbon paper for real cheap. I even have a trick I use. When you hang the flypaper from the ceiling it doesn't really hang down real low and only traps the ones flying up high so I used a regular stick pin and hung a second strip from the one already hanging from the ceiling by sticking the pin into the side of the base, not the bottom, the bottom is too thin to hold it but if you stick it in the side, near the bottom it holds great and now you have two connected that span from the ceiling to about waist level so keep that in mind when doubling them up so as not to place them where you will be bumping into them as they are quite sticky. I really don't like to get less than positive reviews but don't waste your money on this. If you don't like using fly paper then do one of the DIY tricks from youtube with a plastic cup, apple cider, and a bit of saran wrap.

title: Didn't work for me AT ALL
body: I have several fruit flies around the spyder plants in my kitchen (and near a counter at the other end of the kitchen where I have bananas hanging). I bought this with high hopes... but no go. Initially I opened the bottle, placed it between two plants and gave it a few days. Nothing. I then poured it into four small shallow open containers and placed three around all the plants and one near the bananas. Five days later, only 1 fruit fly ended up in any of the containers (I think it got in there by accident & drowned). I can say that after all this time, the smell of apple cider is still very strong. From reading other reviews, it seems that this is either wildly successful or an absolute miss. I'll leave them out for a while longer, but for me, this was a wasted purchase. I had hoped this would have some sort attractant I didn't know about and would work, but could have saved my money and gone back to a plain old cider vinegar & dishsoap mix (which gave me the same result but was much cheaper).

Don't waste your money. I made DIY traps with plastic wrap and holes
